newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Riksbank leaves repo unchanged at 4.10 pc.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Riksbank leaves repo unchanged at 4.10 pc.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, on Tuesday kept its key reverse one-week repo rate unchanged at 4.10 percent.
The decision was in line with expectations with a Reuter poll of 12 economists showing no one expected a cut.

The econmists pointed to the crown's volatility and softness as well as Riksbank governor Urban Backstrom's speech last week, in which he said monetary policy was well measured and that time was needed to evalute effects of previous cuts.
The Riksbank has not cut the repo rate this year, but in 1996 it lowered it to 4.10 percent from 8.91 percent.
The repo will run from March 12 to March 19, the central bank said.

All primary dealers are invited to leave bids by 0900 GMT on March 11. The lowest accepted volume is 200 million crowns ($26.4 million), and the highest accepted volume is 40 billion crowns, the Riksbank said.
The repo will replace a seven-day operation that drained the market of five billion crowns.
